#   `ActionDescriptor`) and `impl From<&DslValue> for serde_json::Value` (real, actively-called
#   JSON-export/UI-boundary bridges, confirmed via `✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio`/`🏭️process` and the

# backs `draw_types::{UiInstance, VectorVertex}` (GPU vertex layout structs with zero `wgpu`-crate
# reference — pure `#[repr(C)]` value types); its own dependency is `bytemuck_derive`, a proc-macro
# that runs on the host at build time and links nothing into the target binary. `semio-framework-job`
# backs `prepared.rs`'s job-driven CPU staging/admission state machine (first-party, itself already
# wasip2-safe). Neither reintroduces the `wasm-bindgen` leak this ticket closes. Ticket

    "dep:wgpu",
    "dep:taffy",
    "dep:js-sys",
    "dep:wasm-bindgen",
    "dep:web-sys",
    "dep:arboard",
    "dep:semio-framework-geometry",
    "dep:semio-framework-job",
    "dep:semio-framework-async",
    "dep:semio-framework-pixels",
]
# 🧬️ Enables the owned TypeScript schema projection for the `wgpu` boundary types.
typegen = ["wgpu"]

[dependencies]
semio-framework-value = { path = "../../../🌱️value/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
ui_styling = { path = "../../🎨️styling/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-styling" }

# ⌨️ Terminal target: semio-styled scene/cell renderer, wasm-safe. Carries no platform I/O on its own.
tui = ["dep:semio-framework-async"]
# 🖥️ Native terminal backend for `tui`: raw mode, alt screen, stdin ANSI input decoding.
tui-terminal = ["tui", "dep:libc"]
# 🌐️ wasm-bindgen exports of the tui `WasmHost` for browser hosts (xterm.js); never default.
tui-bindgen = ["tui", "dep:wasm-bindgen"]

# Names the target, not the `wgpu` crate — that one only arrives with `wgpu-engine` below. `bytemuck`
# backs `draw_types::{UiInstance, VectorVertex}` (GPU vertex layout structs with zero `wgpu`-crate
# reference — pure `#[repr(C)]` value types); its own dependency is `bytemuck_derive`, a proc-macro
# that runs on the host at build time and links nothing into the target binary. `semio-framework-job`
# backs `prepared.rs`'s job-driven CPU staging/admission state machine (first-party, itself already
# wasip2-safe). Neither reintroduces the `wasm-bindgen` leak this ticket closes. Ticket
# 26/09/01/RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS.

# 🎨️ Full retained-mode engine for `wgpu`: arena/tree/layout/text/input/gpu rendering.

    "wgpu",
    "dep:parley",
    "dep:swash",
    "dep:bytemuck",
    "dep:winit",
    "dep:wgpu",
    "dep:taffy",
    "dep:js-sys",
    "dep:wasm-bindgen",
    "dep:web-sys",
    "dep:arboard",
    "dep:semio-framework-geometry",
    "dep:semio-framework-job",
    "dep:semio-framework-async",
    "dep:semio-framework-pixels",
]
# 🧬️ Enables the owned TypeScript schema projection for the `wgpu` boundary types.
typegen = ["wgpu"]

[dependencies]
semio-framework-value = { path = "../../../🌱️value/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
ui_styling = { path = "../../🎨️styling/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-styling" }
# 🎬️ The 15 product scene structs (`World3dScene`/`TableScene`/...) and the generic 3D scene math
# both relocated out of this crate into `semio-framework-ui-scene` — ticket
# 26/08/17/MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME packet `scene-surface`. `component::ui` re-exports
# the former; `kernel_3d_scene` is now a re-export of the latter's `math` module. Non-optional: both
# are re-exported unconditionally from `component::ui`, which itself has no feature gate.
ui_scene = { path = "../../🎬️scene/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-scene" }
# ⛓️ Consumed directly for the `wgpu-engine` widgets that still take `Camera3d` by value (see
# `widgets.rs`); `semio-framework-ui-scene`'s `math` module re-exports `Mat4`/`Vec3` from here too.
semio-framework-geometry = { path = "../../../📐️geometry/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-geometry", optional = true }
semio-framework-job = { path = "../../../🧵️job/📦️packages/🦀️rust", optional = true }
# 🖼️ Owned PNG codec (first-party, its only dependency is the owned DEFLATE module) backing
# `🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu/🖌️paint`'s `🖼️UiImageSources` region: a `Component::Image` whose `src` is a
# `data:image/png` URL decodes in-process instead of showing the placeholder box. No third-party
# image crate enters the graph — see that region's own docstring for the JPEG carve-out.
semio-framework-pixels = { path = "../../../🔲️pixels/📦️packages/🦀️rust", optional = true }
semio-framework-async = { path = "../../../⏳️async/📦️packages/🦀️rust", optional = true }
semio-framework-ui-locale = { path = "../../🌐️locale/📦️packages/🦀️rust", optional = true }
semio-framework-value-derive = { path = "../../../🌱️value/✨️derive/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-value-derive", optional = true }
ui_contract = { path = "../../🧬️contract/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-contract" }
serde = { version = "1.0.219", features = ["derive"], optional = true }
serde_json = { version = "1.0.140", optional = true }

# atlas — versions match what `layout_rs` already resolves in the workspace lockfile (parley
# pulls fontique 0.5.0 transitively; accessed here via `parley::fontique`, not a direct dep).
# `no_std` + `libm` like `ui-render`: embedded font bytes only, no fontique path/mmap sources.

swash = { version = "0.2.6", default-features = false, features = ["render", "std"], optional = true }

[target.'cfg(all(unix, not(target_arch = "wasm32")))'.dependencies]

# 🌉️ Browser-only device/session bindings (`🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu`'s canvas/clipboard/fetch/cursor
# bridges — cursor.rs, prepared.rs, host.rs, text.rs, gpu.rs — plus `tui-bindgen`'s xterm.js

    "WheelEvent",
    "KeyboardEvent",
    "Request",
    "RequestInit",
    "RequestMode",
    "Response",
] }

[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]
wgpu = { version = "29.0.4", default-features = false, features = ["std", "metal", "vulkan", "dx12", "wgsl"], optional = true }

semio-framework-ui-viewport = { path = "../../🪟️viewport/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
tiny-skia = "0.11.4"

id = "plugin"

[lints]
workspace = true

[lib]
path = "🦀️.rs"

[features]
default = []
component-guest = []
component-extension-guest = []
# ⏳️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (W6-A, jobs-runtime → B1 world-collapse): selects the
# guest-side DIRECT host-import path, where a job body awaits `host-async` rather than emitting an
# effect and waiting for its completion event. Since the collapse both paths live in the SAME
# `world actor` (there is no second world), so this gates a calling convention, not a world. It MUST be declared even while no consumer enables it yet —
# an undeclared feature makes every `#[cfg(feature = "component-guest-async")]` block silently unreachable,
# so the code inside is never type-checked by any build (the standing `cfg`-gated-code trap). `JobCtx::host()`
# lives behind exactly this gate.
component-guest-async = []
artifact-app-testing = []

[dependencies]
replication = { package = "semio-framework-replication", path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/📡️replication/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-pack-json = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🎒️pack/🔤️json/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-diagnostic = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/⚠️diagnostic/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-dsl = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🗣️dsl/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-ui-locale = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🌐️locale/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-schema-state = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🧬️schema/📶️state/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-schema-composition = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🧬️schema/🧩️composition/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-schema-registry = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🧬️schema/📇️registry/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-2d = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/◻️2d/📦️packages/🦀️rust", default-features = false }
semio-framework-value = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🌱️value/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework = { path = "../../../../../../../🧰️framework/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework" }
semio-framework-async = { path = "../../../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/⏳️async/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-async" }
semio-framework-job = { path = "../../../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🧵️job/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-job" }
# ⏯️ Tool run contract (ticket 26/09/13/INTERACTIVE-TOOLS-VISIBLE-PROCESS lane W0-D): the runtime ledger/driver
# folds `ToolRunTick`s and publishes one `Edit` at finalize; the pure contract crate never depends back on this one.
semio-framework-tool-run = { workspace = true }
# ⏪️ Non-destructive history editing (ticket 26/09/30/NON-DESTRUCTIVE-HISTORY-EDITING lane W2-A): the per-instance
# `TimeTravelLedger` drives the pure session reducer; the contract crate never depends back on this one.
semio-framework-time-travel = { workspace = true }
# 🎚️ Continuous controls (ticket 26/09/30/NON-DESTRUCTIVE-HISTORY-EDITING lane W3-T2-CONTROLS): every dispatch carrying a
# `gesture` rides the window's `ScrubLedger`; the contract crate never depends back on this one.
semio-framework-tool-machine = { workspace = true }
# 🔤️ First-party RFC 4648 §5 base64url codec: the tool run trace delta rides the scene `toolRunTrace` lane as
# unpadded base64url text (ticket 26/09/13/INTERACTIVE-TOOLS-VISIBLE-PROCESS lane W0-H).
base64_codec = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🚪️io/🔤️base64/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-io-base64" }
# ⏱️ `runtime_live_cleanup_pump`/`runtime_callback_clock_elapsed` judge each maintenance step against
# the interactive-step contract, which this crate calls directly as `semio_framework_trace::…`. The
# call site landed without the manifest edge, so every build of this crate failed on an unlinked crate.
semio-framework-trace = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-hash = { path = "../../../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🔏️hash/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-hash" }
# 🗃️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (sdk-dedyn, O1): `#[dyn_enum]` on `trait PluginApp` —
# each fleet plugin crate closes its own per-plugin app enum via `dyn_enum_close!` (cross-crate,
# see 📓️terra-dyn-enum-macro-report.md's recipe §5).
semio-framework-dispatch-macros = { path = "../../../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🔀️dispatch/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-dispatch-macros" }
semio-framework-os-kernel = { path = "../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-kernel" }
# 🧩️ UNIFIED-COMPOSABLE-ARTIFACT-SYSTEM (C1): `ArtifactChildren`'s `slots() -> &'static
# [ChildSlotSpec]` needs the real `ChildSlotSpec`/ `ArtifactCompositionFields` types A2 landed in
# this crate — not otherwise reachable from `semio-framework-plugin` (`semio-framework` itself does
# not depend on `semio-framework-schema`). No cycle: `semio-framework-schema` depends only on
# `semio-framework-os-kernel` + its own derive crate, never on this crate or `semio-framework`.
semio-framework-schema = { path = "../../../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🧬️schema/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-schema" }
# 🧬️ The semantic UI contract and its headless runtime replace `ui_wgpu`'s node types here: both are
# dependency-light (serde + styling tokens) and compile for wasm32-wasip2, where the old dependency
# dragged a whole render engine into every guest.
# 🏷️ Still needed for the NON-node types the ui crate owns — app labels, context-menu requests,
# window measures, world3d camera helpers. Those are separate domains from the node schema this
# program replaced, so they keep their home; the "wgpu" feature is declarative types only and
# stays wasm32-wasip2-safe (it never pulls the engine, which lives behind "wgpu-engine").
ui_wgpu = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui", features = ["wgpu"] }
semio_framework_ui_contract = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🧬️contract/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-contract" }
semio_framework_ui_runtime = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🧠️runtime/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-runtime" }
# 🧬️ M2 fallout (ticket 26/08/17 `design-unified.md`, terra-sdk-wire): the `scene-surface` packet
# relocated the 15 product scene structs (`TableScene`, `World3dScene`, …) plus their helpers
# (`world3d_default_selection_json`) out of `ui_wgpu::wgpu` into this new crate — `ui_wgpu` no
# longer re-exports them, so this SDK needs the dependency directly to keep compiling.
semio_framework_ui_scene = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🎬️scene/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-scene" }
serde = { version = "1.0.219", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.140"
# 🪶️ RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS (26/09/01): default features drop
# `bitflags` — `world actor`'s WIT (`🧬️schema/📜️.wit`) declares no `flags` type, so wit-bindgen's
# generated code never calls into it; confirmed dead (one leftover generic-instantiation symbol,
# no real function) in the built `.wasm` before this change. `async`/`std`/`realloc`/`macro-string`
# stay: `poll` is `async func` in the WIT and genuinely exercises `wit_bindgen::rt::async_support`
# (266 distinct linked symbols observed in a built component). See
# `🔍️research/📓️wit-bindgen-guest-surface.md`.
wit-bindgen = { version = "0.57.1", default-features = false, features = ["macros", "realloc", "async", "std", "macro-string"] }
# 🌱️ RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS (26/09/01): `ArtifactApp::Snapshot`/
# `Config`/`Draft`/`Presence`/`Transient` now bound on `ToValue`/`FromValue` instead of
# `Serialize`/`DeserializeOwned` (`../../📦️packages/🦀️rust/🦀️.rs`'s trait definitions). Promoted from
# `[dev-dependencies]` because the crate's own production defaults (`NoConfig`/`NoPresence`/
# `NoTransient`, `crate::local_interaction`'s `InteractionConfigMutation`) derive `ToValue`/
# `FromValue` directly now, not only the test fixtures.
semio-framework-value-derive = { path = "../../../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🌱️value/✨️derive/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-value-derive" }

[dev-dependencies]
semio-framework-async-macros = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/⏳️async/✨️macros/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
# 🚪️ Test-only `entrypoint`: `one_framework_reserved_route_fits_a_bounded_thread_stack` drives one
# `interactionSelect` on a deliberately small OS thread, and only `block_on` can pump a future from
# inside a `std::thread` the test spawned itself (the `#[async_test]` executor is bound to libtest's
# own thread). Dev-only, so no interactive-reachable build ever sees the gate open.
semio-framework-async = { path = "../../../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/⏳️async/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-async", features = ["entrypoint"] }
wasmtime = { version = "47.0.3", features = ["cranelift"] }

# 🎭️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (B1-host-native): `GuestRuntime`'s `RuntimeActorId`/
# `PackageId`/`PackageHash` vocabulary (design-runtime.md §2) — packet A1's pure, domain-neutral
# actor crate, already a `[workspace.dependencies]` entry.
semio-framework-actor = { workspace = true }

semio-framework-async = { workspace = true, features = ["entrypoint"] }
semio-framework-job = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-os-services = { workspace = true }

# violation instead of silently absorbed — see `📓️p1c-actor-shards.md`.

# `AsyncActorTask` is one `tokio::spawn`ed task per actor, coordinated with its caller over
# `tokio::sync::{mpsc,oneshot}` — the ONLY tokio surface this crate needs. `["sync", "rt"]` only:
# tokio itself stays OWNED by `semio-framework-os-services` (the ticket's binding tokio-routing
# rule) — this crate must never construct a `tokio::Runtime`; `tokio::spawn`/`JoinHandle` run
# against whatever `Handle` is current when a caller enters it, injected from outside, never built
# here. `rt-multi-thread` is deliberately NOT enabled — building a scheduler is exactly what this

wasmtime = { version = "47.0.3", features = ["cranelift", "component-model", "component-model-async"] }

serde = { version = "1.0.219", features = ["derive"] }

semio-framework-hash = { path = "../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🔏️hash/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }

[dev-dependencies]
semio-framework-async-macros = { path = "../../../../../../../🔨️modules/⏳️async/✨️macros/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
# 🧪️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (terra-effects-async): `testkit` (unions with the

semio-framework-async = { workspace = true, features = ["testkit"] }

    "🛂️proctor/📦️packages/🦀️rust",
]
exclude = ["**/🏅️standards/**", "**/🔮️oracles/**", "**/👽️guest/**"]

[workspace.metadata.semio.repository]
schema-version = 1
member-manifests = ["**/📦️packages/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml"]

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.95"

[workspace.dependencies]
semio-framework-replication = { path = "../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/📡️replication/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-server = { path = "../🧰️framework/🛍️products/🖥️server/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-quiz = { path = "../🧰️framework/🛍️products/❓️quiz/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-async = { path = "../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/⏳️async/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-dispatch-macros = { path = "../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🔀️dispatch/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-hash = { path = "../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🔏️hash/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
serde = { version = "1.0.228", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = { version = "1.0.149", features = ["raw_value"] }
wasm-bindgen = "0.2.106"
js-sys = "0.3.83"
tokio = { version = "1" }

# 🧭️ Internal path deps for crates that exist TODAY at their current location, surveyed
# by counting `path = "…"` dependency references across all Cargo.toml files (>5 other
# manifests). Not wired to any member yet — a later wave can adopt `.workspace = true` as
# a drop-in, or repoint ONE line here when a crate merges/moves instead of editing every
# consumer. `# N refs` is the survey count. Grouped: os-kernel/core, math, ui, plugin-internal.
# ---- core (24) ----
[profile.dev]
debug = false
incremental = false

[profile.dev.build-override]
opt-level = 3

# ⚡️ The plugin runtime every native dev host embeds (the semio MCP gateway, the hub, native shells) is
# optimized even in the dev profile. At `opt-level = 0` the wasmtime component-model machinery around
# every guest crossing and host call, and cranelift compiling a 129 MB wasm-dev guest, dominated the
# guest's own work. Measured on the wfc genesis `inference_run` over the semio MCP: 112.7 s with this
# set unoptimized vs 63.9 s optimized (ticket 26/09/23, `📓️wp-g5.md`), and a first solve after a guest
# rebuild waited ~9 min for its unoptimized cranelift compile. Only these crates change, so a rebuild
# costs their own compile plus a relink of their dependents (1 min 44 s measured).
[profile.dev.package.wasmtime]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-environ]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-core]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-cranelift]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-fiber]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-unwinder]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-cache]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-component-util]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-jit-debug]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-jit-icache-coherence]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-wasi]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-wasi-io]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-codegen]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-frontend]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-entity]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-bforest]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-bitset]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-control]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-native]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-codegen-shared]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-assembler-x64]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.regalloc2]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmparser]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.pulley-interpreter]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.gimli]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.object]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wit-parser]
opt-level = 3

# 🧮️ The owned wasm interpreter (`semio-framework-plugin-host::interpreter`) runs every trusted-catalog
# verification `codec.pack-schema-hash` on the hub's startup path. At `opt-level = 0` a debug hub spent
# >11 min of one core interpreting writer/draw/puzzle during catalog load and the candidate readiness
# wait gave up (ticket 26/09/23 W1 §4.6, sampled: 100 % in `CoreInstance::execute_machine`).
[profile.dev.package.semio-framework-plugin-host]
opt-level = 3

# 🔐️ The repository's own SHA-256 carries every hub credential check: a sign-in derives PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256
# at 210 000 iterations. At `opt-level = 0` one derivation took ~2 s on an idle debug hub and 8.5 s on hub
# 7800 under load (ticket 26/09/23 H9 session 12), all inside the compression function; optimizing this
# one small crate makes a dev hub's sign-in cost what a release hub's does.
[profile.dev.package.semio-framework-hash]
opt-level = 3

# 🛡️ WASI component links alone select this mitigation for rust-lld's ElemSection crash.
# Native dev retains Cargo's parallel codegen policy; publication stays wasm-release.
[profile.wasm-dev]
inherits = "dev"
codegen-units = 1
# 🧾️ A component's described bytes must be its shipped bytes: `describe` and `component-dev` link the same
# `cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib` unit, and `incremental` is part of that unit's profile identity, so an
# inherited `incremental = true` split it by the caller's `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` into two compiles with two
# different wasm hashes (ticket 26/09/23 W1: descriptor `ce48…`/`2a5c…` vs staged `a740…`).
incremental = false

# 🎚️ The plugin guest must meet the framework's 8 ms interactive-step contract even in the dev
# profile: at `opt-level = 0` a lowpoly render turn tessellates its seeded mesh in 10-11.5 ms and
# the runtime traps it with `plugin.internal.interactive-ceiling`, so the window renders a fault
# instead of geometry. Scoped to this package rather than raised on the whole profile because the
# io layer (`semio-s-plugin-stdio`) is not on the render path and is far more expensive to compile.
[profile.wasm-dev.package.semio-framework-os-flow]
opt-level = 2

# 🎚️ `Evaluator::evaluate_channels_budgeted` — the topological dag walk itself, run once per hop.
[profile.wasm-dev.package.semio-framework-os-kernel-neural-engine]
opt-level = 2

# 🎚️ `DslValue`/`OrderedMap` — the per-neuron `Dictionary` every walk clones, merges and hashes.
[profile.wasm-dev.package.semio-framework-replication]
opt-level = 2

# 🎚️ `pack::json` — the codec that serializes each node's input/output payload on the same hop.
[profile.wasm-dev.package.semio-framework-pack]
opt-level = 2

# 🎚️ Answers `capability: evaluate`/`tessellate` for the BREP operators the example drives.
[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = "debuginfo"
incremental = false
trim-paths = "object"

# 🪶️ REDUCE-DEMONSTRATOR-IDLE-MEMORY-FOOTPRINT. wasm32-wasip2 plugin components only — os-dev's
# 📜️script.ts passes `--profile wasm-release` when building plugin crates. Inherits ship-oriented
# `[profile.release]` above, then overrides for wasm size/runtime (see below).
#
# - opt-level "s" (not "z"): "z" measurably slows hot numeric loops in geometry/FEM solvers for a
#   few extra percent of size; the wasm-opt -Oz post-pass (see buildPlugin/transpilePluginComponent)
#   gets the "z"-class shrink without paying that runtime cost in every plugin.
# - lto "thin" (not "fat"): fat LTO re-links ~25 plugin cdylibs individually — 2-4x slower per plugin
#   for a low single-digit percent size gain over thin. Thin still gets full cross-crate inlining.
# - codegen-units = 1: maximizes cross-crate dedup/inlining and also sidesteps the LLVM-22
#   ElemSection::writeBody crash noted above (a stable low CGU count, same fix as `store`'s override).
# - strip = "symbols": drops the wasm `name` custom section, which is pure debug/dev-tooling weight
#   (measured ~14MB on the largest single plugin, ~87MB across the built fleet) never used at runtime.
# - incremental = false: deterministic output; release units are rebuilt whole anyway, so incremental
#   session state would only cost disk in the shared build-dir (`.cargo/config.toml` `build.build-dir`).
# - trim-paths = "object": strips absolute build-host cargo-registry paths retained in panic
#   `Location` strings (panic = "unwind" is intentionally NOT overridden here — wasm32-wasip2's
#   target spec already defaults to panic-strategy "abort", so plugins already abort-on-panic and
#   `catch_unwind` already never catches on this target; setting it explicitly would be a no-op).
[profile.wasm-release]
inherits = "release"
opt-level = "s"
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = "symbols"
incremental = false
trim-paths = "object"

# Explicit: profile inheritance does NOT inherit package-specific overrides from the parent
# profile, so without this `store` would fall back to workspace defaults under `wasm-release`.
[profile.wasm-release.package.semio-framework-os-kernel]
codegen-units = 1

# 🧹️ RUST-WIDE-CLEAN-REFACTOR-CAMPAIGN baseline. Kept at "warn" (never "deny") in
# the manifest so live concurrent edits never hard-break; zero-warning is enforced
# at verification gates via `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`. NEVER set RUSTFLAGS to
# add -D warnings — it replaces (not merges) .cargo/config.toml's rustflags.
[workspace.lints.rust]
future_incompatible = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
rust_2018_idioms = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn = "warn"
unused_lifetimes = "warn"
unused_qualifications = "warn"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
cloned_instead_of_copied = "warn"
inefficient_to_string = "warn"
map_unwrap_or = "warn"
needless_pass_by_value = "warn"
semicolon_if_nothing_returned = "warn"
unnecessary_wraps = "warn"
redundant_clone = "warn"
# phase B (enable after the T2/T3 waves land): unwrap_used = "warn"

# 🧭️ Internal path deps for crates that exist TODAY at their current location, surveyed
# by counting `path = "…"` dependency references across all Cargo.toml files (>5 other
# manifests). Not wired to any member yet — a later wave can adopt `.workspace = true` as
# a drop-in, or repoint ONE line here when a crate merges/moves instead of editing every
# consumer. `# N refs` is the survey count. Grouped: os-kernel/core, math, ui, plugin-internal.
# ---- core (24) ----
[profile.dev]
debug = false
incremental = false

[profile.dev.build-override]
opt-level = 3

# ⚡️ The plugin runtime every native dev host embeds (the semio MCP gateway, the hub, native shells) is
# optimized even in the dev profile. At `opt-level = 0` the wasmtime component-model machinery around
# every guest crossing and host call, and cranelift compiling a 129 MB wasm-dev guest, dominated the
# guest's own work. Measured on the wfc genesis `inference_run` over the semio MCP: 112.7 s with this
# set unoptimized vs 63.9 s optimized (ticket 26/09/23, `📓️wp-g5.md`), and a first solve after a guest
# rebuild waited ~9 min for its unoptimized cranelift compile. Only these crates change, so a rebuild
# costs their own compile plus a relink of their dependents (1 min 44 s measured).
[profile.dev.package.wasmtime]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-environ]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-core]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-cranelift]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-fiber]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-unwinder]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-cache]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-component-util]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-jit-debug]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-internal-jit-icache-coherence]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-wasi]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.wasmtime-wasi-io]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-codegen]

[profile.dev.package.cranelift-frontend]

# 🧮️ The owned wasm interpreter (`semio-framework-plugin-host::interpreter`) runs every trusted-catalog
# verification `codec.pack-schema-hash` on the hub's startup path. At `opt-level = 0` a debug hub spent
# >11 min of one core interpreting writer/draw/puzzle during catalog load and the candidate readiness
# wait gave up (ticket 26/09/23 W1 §4.6, sampled: 100 % in `CoreInstance::execute_machine`).
[profile.dev.package.semio-framework-plugin-host]
opt-level = 3

# 🔐️ The repository's own SHA-256 carries every hub credential check: a sign-in derives PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256
# at 210 000 iterations. At `opt-level = 0` one derivation took ~2 s on an idle debug hub and 8.5 s on hub
# 7800 under load (ticket 26/09/23 H9 session 12), all inside the compression function; optimizing this
# one small crate makes a dev hub's sign-in cost what a release hub's does.
[profile.dev.package.semio-framework-hash]
opt-level = 3

# 🛡️ WASI component links alone select this mitigation for rust-lld's ElemSection crash.
# Native dev retains Cargo's parallel codegen policy; publication stays wasm-release.
[profile.wasm-dev]
inherits = "dev"
codegen-units = 1
# 🧾️ A component's described bytes must be its shipped bytes: `describe` and `component-dev` link the same
# `cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib` unit, and `incremental` is part of that unit's profile identity, so an
# inherited `incremental = true` split it by the caller's `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` into two compiles with two
# different wasm hashes (ticket 26/09/23 W1: descriptor `ce48…`/`2a5c…` vs staged `a740…`).
incremental = false

# 🎚️ The plugin guest must meet the framework's 8 ms interactive-step contract even in the dev
# profile: at `opt-level = 0` a lowpoly render turn tessellates its seeded mesh in 10-11.5 ms and
# the runtime traps it with `plugin.internal.interactive-ceiling`, so the window renders a fault
# instead of geometry. Scoped to this package rather than raised on the whole profile because the
# io layer (`semio-s-plugin-stdio`) is not on the render path and is far more expensive to compile.
[profile.wasm-dev.package.semio-framework-os-flow]
opt-level = 2

# 🎚️ `Evaluator::evaluate_channels_budgeted` — the topological dag walk itself, run once per hop.
[profile.wasm-dev.package.semio-framework-os-kernel-neural-engine]
opt-level = 2

# 🎚️ `DslValue`/`OrderedMap` — the per-neuron `Dictionary` every walk clones, merges and hashes.
[profile.wasm-dev.package.semio-framework-replication]
opt-level = 2

# 🎚️ `pack::json` — the codec that serializes each node's input/output payload on the same hop.
[profile.wasm-dev.package.semio-framework-pack]
opt-level = 2

# 🎚️ Answers `capability: evaluate`/`tessellate` for the BREP operators the example drives.
[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = "debuginfo"
incremental = false
trim-paths = "object"

# 🪶️ REDUCE-DEMONSTRATOR-IDLE-MEMORY-FOOTPRINT. wasm32-wasip2 plugin components only — os-dev's
# 📜️script.ts passes `--profile wasm-release` when building plugin crates. Inherits ship-oriented
# `[profile.release]` above, then overrides for wasm size/runtime (see below).
#
# - opt-level "s" (not "z"): "z" measurably slows hot numeric loops in geometry/FEM solvers for a
#   few extra percent of size; the wasm-opt -Oz post-pass (see buildPlugin/transpilePluginComponent)
#   gets the "z"-class shrink without paying that runtime cost in every plugin.
# - lto "thin" (not "fat"): fat LTO re-links ~25 plugin cdylibs individually — 2-4x slower per plugin
#   for a low single-digit percent size gain over thin. Thin still gets full cross-crate inlining.
# - codegen-units = 1: maximizes cross-crate dedup/inlining and also sidesteps the LLVM-22
#   ElemSection::writeBody crash noted above (a stable low CGU count, same fix as `store`'s override).
# - strip = "symbols": drops the wasm `name` custom section, which is pure debug/dev-tooling weight
#   (measured ~14MB on the largest single plugin, ~87MB across the built fleet) never used at runtime.
# - incremental = false: deterministic output; release units are rebuilt whole anyway, so incremental
#   session state would only cost disk in the shared build-dir (`.cargo/config.toml` `build.build-dir`).
# - trim-paths = "object": strips absolute build-host cargo-registry paths retained in panic
#   `Location` strings (panic = "unwind" is intentionally NOT overridden here — wasm32-wasip2's
#   target spec already defaults to panic-strategy "abort", so plugins already abort-on-panic and
#   `catch_unwind` already never catches on this target; setting it explicitly would be a no-op).
[profile.wasm-release]
inherits = "release"
opt-level = "s"
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = "symbols"
incremental = false
trim-paths = "object"

# Explicit: profile inheritance does NOT inherit package-specific overrides from the parent
# profile, so without this `store` would fall back to workspace defaults under `wasm-release`.
[profile.wasm-release.package.semio-framework-os-kernel]
codegen-units = 1

# 🧹️ RUST-WIDE-CLEAN-REFACTOR-CAMPAIGN baseline. Kept at "warn" (never "deny") in
# the manifest so live concurrent edits never hard-break; zero-warning is enforced
# at verification gates via `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`. NEVER set RUSTFLAGS to
# add -D warnings — it replaces (not merges) .cargo/config.toml's rustflags.
[workspace.lints.rust]
future_incompatible = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
rust_2018_idioms = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn = "warn"
unused_lifetimes = "warn"
unused_qualifications = "warn"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
cloned_instead_of_copied = "warn"
inefficient_to_string = "warn"
map_unwrap_or = "warn"
needless_pass_by_value = "warn"
semicolon_if_nothing_returned = "warn"
unnecessary_wraps = "warn"
redundant_clone = "warn"
# phase B (enable after the T2/T3 waves land): unwrap_used = "warn"
